body:
## Summary

- TestAdoptWatchlistEntriesIsIdempotentAndNeverOverwrites and TestAdoptWatchlistEntriesCarriesAnUpgradeIntact mutated a file-backed DefinitionsStore and returned without flushing, so the write-behind writer's asynchronous save could still be in flight when eachBackend's t.TempDir() was removed at subtest teardown -- racing RemoveAll. This is what failed on PR #473's CI (a frontend-only diff) with `TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat ...: directory not empty`.
- Verified the hypothesis before fixing: StateStore/DefinitionsStore already expose Close/Flush for exactly this, and every other write-behind test in internal/engine already calls flushDefinitionsForTest/flushForTest before its own teardown. These two tests were the only omissions in the whole package -- not a missing product capability, a missing call to an existing one.
- Added the missing flushDefinitionsForTest calls to both tests, and added a permanent regression test (TestAdoptWatchlistEntriesTeardownDoesNotRaceAPendingWrite) that runs the same mutation sequence in a tight loop immediately followed by the same os.RemoveAll a TempDir cleanup performs -- pinning that a flush before removal is unconditionally safe.

Closes #474

## How this was verified as a real race, not assumed

- `go test -race -run TestAdoptWatchlistEntriesIsIdempotentAndNeverOverwrites -count=500 ./internal/engine` did not reproduce the failure -- the race window is narrower than this sandbox's scheduler naturally produces through go test's own per-subtest overhead.
- Reproduced it directly instead: the same AdoptWatchlistEntries + UpdateExpectation sequence against a real file backend, immediately followed by os.RemoveAll of the same directory (bypassing go test's indirection). Without a flush in between, this failed with the exact `unlinkat ...: directory not empty` signature -- 3 failures reproduced at 3000 iterations/run across 3 runs when the flush was intentionally removed for this proof. With the flush restored, 10 consecutive runs (2000 iterations total) passed cleanly.
- The committed regression test runs 200 iterations, which is the version described above with the flush in place.

## Test plan

- [x] gofmt -l against every tracked .go file -- empty
- [x] go vet ./... -- clean
- [x] go test ./... -- all packages pass
- [x] go test -race -count=20 ./internal/engine -- passes (173.8s)
- [x] go test -race -count=20 ./internal/store -- passes (unaffected package, no write-behind usage there at all)
title: Fix #474: flush DefinitionsStore before adopt tests' TempDir teardown
